DIE XENO SCUM

FOR THE EMPEROR

FOR THE ULTRAMARINES

I had a lot of fun with this game and for me it's the best Alien action game since Monolith's AvP2. Very atmospheric thanks to the appealing visuals and soundtrack are gratifying. 
The satisfying shooting mechanics and  concocted system of levelling/modifying weapons/classes alone makes this game worth checking.  A very nice touch is modifying the missions parameters through the unlockable decks of cards with random properties: the more they raise the difficulty of the mission, the greater the reward for the player. 
Speaking of mods, perks and cosmetics, there is a whole bunch of them and fortunately, acquiring them is not intrusive. 
The objectives in the campaign mode are painfully schematic and the levels are sadly linear but the relentless escalating Xenos attacks and the constant feeling of being threatened by them let quickly you forget about that, especially if you play with other players. Plus the levels are strewn with a lot of new canonical pieces of information to the Alien universe and references to the other Alien franchise media, which probably every fan of the franchise will appreciate.
good story solid gameplay hope to see more, it seems to lack a little content but its still great and well thought out. worth buying, fantastic entry, full of nostalgia.

To start: The game is NOT worth the $40 they're asking for it. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE!

I bought this game at 50% off and was pleasantly surprised by how much fun I had playing it. There are a lot of fun things that cause me to keep playing and changing up my play style:

- There are loads of weapons and attachments, providing a variety of builds in conjunction with class perks.

- Gun play feels fun and individual weapons feel lovely in their sound design, handling, and impact.

- Perks work on a kind of Tetris puzzle like system (or the limited Resident Evil inventory if you're more familiar with that), wherein certain perks have certain shapes on a grid, and some perks require adjacency to another specific perk in order to function. While some may find this convoluted and/or annoying, it is extremely satisfying to me to maximize the perks I want by playing a small puzzle game.

- The enemies are in their own faction, so you'll have three-way fights between you, synths, and xenomorphs.

With all that good stuff said, there are some hefty flaws with this game that make it not fun for the vast majority of people:

- The game is all about grinding. Your character, your class, and your weapons all have levels. You will be replaying the same missions over and over, simply to level the things you want so that they're actually useful at higher difficulties (where it becomes more fun).

- Semi related to the previous point, all unlocks are random. So it's entirely possible to get a bunch of weapons you don't like or attachments for gun types you never use before you can find something enjoyable.

- The AI is notoriously poor. Xenomorphs of every type (except the Spitter) will spawn and do nothing but charge the player in a straight line, usually single file into the meat grinder. They act more like dogs than apex killing machines. They will not double back and try to outflank you, seek shelter from bullets, or sprint faster towards you if they have no other choice. They are predictable and exploitable. Your AI companions (if you play without friends) are unreliable. They will frequently refuse to fire, miss when they do fire, and throw grenades at their feet.

- Related to the previous point, perhaps the AI can't fully be blamed for its failings due to the fact that almost every level and area you fight is a tunnel of some kind with you on one end and xenos on the other. Sometimes you'll be in the center of an X, but xenos will only spawn from one tunnel at a time, making the whole ordeal nothing more than shooting xenos in a barrel.

- Max player count is (literally) oddly 3.

- Enemies are poorly utilized. This point will spoil some xenos enemy types for you so, if you like surprises, skip this point.
;;;;;Runners are the basic xenos you will encounter, and suffer the most from Dog AI Syndrome: they will attack in swarms from a single direction. 
;;;;;Bursters are a variant of runners whose heads glow bright green. They will explode upon death, dealing damage in a small area. Unfortunately, they act just like Runners and even spawn alongside them but in few numbers, making them easy priority targets who almost never get to pop off near a team.
;;;;;Spitters suffer the least from poor AI because their AI only tells them to get into cover and attack from range. What prevents the Spitters from being more effective is their slow fire rate and the fact that some (thankfully not a lot) of their hiding places just so happen to house an easily shot exploding canister, making fighting them either unimportant or very easy.
;;;;;Prowlers, in my opinion, got the short end of the stick. They're designed to be ambush units, lying in wait for the player whom they will grab and pin down as they tear into you. The problem is that, while waiting, they breath incredibly loud, giving away their position minutes before you actually see them. Additionally, your character will often call out the presence of a Prowler in case its breathing didn't clue you in enough, even if your character can't see the Prowler. Finally, in replaying missions over and over, you'll come to learn that there are only a few spots Prowlers can spawn in, making these specialized units underutilized and heavily ineffective.
;;;;;Drones are the first big bad xenos. Their flaws are only apparent once you've leveled up enough to do lots of damage to them in a short amount of time. Drones are the typical xenomorph from the movie. They're designed to harass and tackle you like the Prowler before disappearing into a vent to do the whole thing over. Unfortunately, they're tall and lumbering, making them easy to hit. Once you get them down to half health, they will immediately stop whatever it is their doing (even walking towards you) and will make a beeline for the nearest vent to try for another go at you from a different angle, usually only a few seconds later. So, especially with better weapons, perks, and attachments to your name, it's often the case that a Drone will spawn, walk towards you, be brought down to half health, immediately turn around, and die before it can even attack you.
;;;;;Poppers are headcrabs only encountered in the later levels. Like Bursters, they explode, but they're not mixed in with any other units. Unfortunately, they suffer from Dog AI Syndrome and skitter single file towards you in small amounts, slowly.

- Horde Mode, the main reason I got the game, is locked behind the campaign. Granted you can beat the campaign on the easiest difficulty, but still.

- Horde Mode isn't as fun as I was expecting it to be due to many of the aforementioned problems. Enemies progressively get beefed up, but that's it. Their AI is still poor, and the lack of variety when it comes to xenomorph types becomes much more noticeable.

- Doc (the medic) isn't viable at high levels of difficulty due to the way their healing ability works. Unlike being on a cooldown like every other ability, theirs has a charge that can only be refilled by picking up medkits, which give you less charge than you would get health from just using the medkit. Additionally, the charge is very low. I suppose they intend the tradeoff to be a medkit without having to stop shooting, but what it ends up as is an ability you can no longer use halfway through the mission.

- The max mouse sensitivity is 2.5. This is too slow for me, but I have a mouse that lets me bypass that. Oddly enough, the game also contains mouse acceleration, so be prepared to suddenly turn 720* when you try fighting the mouse to turn faster.

- Challenge cards are a neat way to play. Everyone can select one challenge card for a campaign mission. Unfortunately, the game only applies a single card at random, removing so much depth and replayability for a grinding campaign.

IN SUMMARY:
If you want quick casual fun with high customization and you have at least one other friend willing to play it with you, get this game on sale.

If you're looking for a tactical class based shooter that forces you to think on your toes or gives you a challenge, look elsewhere.

This game is a weird but awesome gem among the sea of ambitious but objectively mixed releases the past couple years. This game is straightforward but fun and filled with all sorts of different weapons and cosmetics. All without any sort of microtransactions! My main criticism is the same as everyone else's, and it's that there's a relatively limited number of modes and levels. But even then it's still a lot of fun. I highly recommend.

Also, if the developer is reading this: Please give us the class M41. I love the M41A2 in game but getting the classic original with movie-accurate stats would be nuts in the best way!
